claims.statement: The gating supply-chain scan is decided in pure Python over osv-scanner's `--format json` output, never by the scanner's exit code, because osv-scanner exits 1 on ANY finding and offers no severity flag; `_run` never raises on a non-zero scanner exit and `gate(osv_json)` is the only HIGH decision point, returning every finding id whose max CVSS >= HIGH (7.0).

osv-scanner's `severity[].score` is a CVSS vector string, not a number: `_max_cvss` accepts a numeric score directly, otherwise computes the CVSS v3 base score from the vector via `_cvss3_base` (FIRST.org metric tables; unparseable or CVSS v2 vectors yield None), and falls back to the qualitative `database_specific.severity` label band (`_LABEL_SCORE`, where HIGH maps to 8.0) when no CVSS is parseable.

A HIGH+ (CVSS >= 7.0) finding aborts the online scan with `ScanError` (exit 1 from the CLI), while lower findings are returned as `ScanResult.warnings` and printed without failing; osv-scanner's exit 128 ("no package sources found") becomes its own investigate-warning rather than a pass or a failure, and every scanner invocation in scan.py is bounded at `_TIMEOUT = 300` seconds.

Two complementary per-image scan passes exist: a credentialed in-image scan (`_scan_image_in_container`, running the baked `harnessed-scan` in a throwaway container with token env files injected) that is ADVISORY and never gates, and an online archive scan (`podman save` to a tar, then `run_image_scan_online`) that GATES on HIGH+; `_scan_image` runs both and returns clean only when both are clean.

`harnessed build` is deliberately credential-free (`_build_derived_image` never passes a secret), so snyk and socket — the token-gated scanners — only ever run under the credentialed pass; the derived Dockerfile has had no scan layer at all since the tools/install steps moved out of image layers into per-stack volumes, because that layer scanned an image with no stack content while still printing a green-looking result.

`harnessed rescan [image]` re-scans one named image or every image carrying the `harnessed=true` label (set by `_build_derived_image` for exactly this purpose); the image listing goes through `_listing` and is load-bearing because an unanswered listing would print "nothing to rescan", exit 0, and silently skip the whole nightly. `harnessed scan <stack> [harness]` scopes the same `_scan_image` to one stack, fanning out over built harnesses; `build --no-security-scans` (`HARNESSED_NO_SCANS=true`) skips the credentialed pass and `_surface_scan_report` then says nothing was scanned.

The nightly rescan is driven by `systemd/harnessed-rescan.timer` (OnCalendar=daily, Persistent=true) firing `~/.local/bin/harnessed rescan` via a oneshot service; the timer requires `loginctl enable-linger` (the user systemd instance is torn down on logout without it) and network egress to osv.dev at scan time — the online DB is the whole point, since a stale-DB nightly sees nothing new forever.

The scan timeout ladder is deliberately layered: per-scanner 120s (env `HARNESSED_SCAN_TIMEOUT`, `timeout -k 10`), a 900s backstop over the whole scan container, and a 1800s bound on the online archive scan — the online bound is larger AND bounded precisely because nobody watches an unattended hang, which would wedge the timer silently and look exactly like a nightly that keeps finding nothing.

`harnessed-scan` always exits 0 (advisory, never gating) and makes coverage first-class: every scanner announces an attempt to a ledger before running, a manifest line is written only for parseable output, and the summary distinguishes `no-output` (ran, probably broken) from `unrun` (never started — no token, absent binary, timeout, nothing to scan, with the recorded reason); an unrun line beats a bare attempt for the same (tool, source), a pair that both reported and skipped yields only the skip so partial findings never reach the totals, and zero reporting scanners prints NO COVERAGE rather than a reassuring zero.

The in-image osv pass encodes osv-scanner's exit-code contract verified against 2.5.1: 128 ("No package sources found") is recorded as a reasoned skip because falling through would write no manifest line and read as a broken scanner, while 127 deliberately keeps falling through since a broken invocation is what that bucket is for; and any early bail a scanner itself knows about must call `record_skip` before returning, because an attempt with no result and no reason reads as "ran and produced nothing".

The attempts/manifest ledgers are a hand-rolled `|`-separated format with no escaping, parsed by `split("|", 3)`; the bash writer strips `|` from every field at a single choke point (`nosep`) because one scanner label is `recipe: $(basename …)` — a directory name a recipe controls — and the Python parser deliberately does not depend on that guarantee, with maxsplit=3 keeping the whole tail as the reason.

Advisories with no patched release anywhere upstream are ACKNOWLEDGED, not suppressed: the list is keyed by advisory ID (self-expiring — a fixed release stops emitting the id) with the package name as a second necessary condition that can only narrow, never a package-name key; every hit is counted, printed by name, and written to scan-report.json while being excluded from the totals.

Scanner output is untrusted third-party input reaching a build console and scan-report.json, so the summarizer sanitizes at both sinks (printable-filtered, length-bounded package names and advisory ids), handles snyk's `identifiers` defensively against non-list JSON shapes, and counts an id-less finding under a synthetic key rather than dropping it (a silent under-count is the one failure direction a security scan must never take) — because the surrounding bash runs `set -uo pipefail` without `-e`, a Python exception would leave the script exiting 0 with no report at all.

Scanner tokens are env-only (never a build-arg, so never baked into image history) and resolved on the HOST from the user-global `~/.config/harnessed/.env.schema` via varlock or a bare `.env` (`_resolve_launch_secrets(project_path=None)`), handed to podman as a mode-0600 temp `--env-file` unlinked afterwards; varlock never runs in-container, project env is deliberately not layered in, a tokenless run explicitly says snyk and socket sat out, and socket derives its org slug from the token (an explicit `SOCKET_CLI_ORG_SLUG` wins) since a container has no ~/.config/socket.

The launcher surfaces the CREDENTIALED scan report as authoritative (`keep_existing`): overwriting it with the image-baked, credential-free report would replace snyk/socket findings with a report that structurally cannot contain them — the exact failure that once produced a green "no high/critical" verdict on a build that had just reported 4 high; the credentialed scan container is therefore kept just long enough to `cp` the report out rather than run with `--rm`, and the build unlinks any previous scan-report.json before the re-scan so an old report cannot pass for this scan's output.

The base image bakes the four scanners plus the scan script once (`mise use -g uv osv-scanner`, `uv tool install pip-audit`, `pnpm add -g snyk socket`), COPYing `catalog/base/harnessed-scan` to `/usr/local/bin/harnessed-scan`, so `rescan` needs no network install and the advisory in-image scan always has its tools available.

The gating online archive scan is executed HOST-side: `_scan_image` runs `podman save` and then a host subprocess `uv run --no-project --quiet --with ruamel.yaml python -m harnessed.cli scan-image-online <tar>` (the tar unlinked in a `finally`) — no daemon-in-container and no API socket — so the throwaway container the credentialed advisory pass creates is the only container involved in a rescan, and no scanner token is ever resolved from inside an image layer.

The build's post-build credentialed scan mounts the per-stack volumes into the scan container (`extra_args`, with `_ensure_stack_volumes` populating them BEFORE the scan and before the settings merge), so the report covers what launch actually installs — an image-only scan would still pass and still print green while silently covering less — while `_scan_image` (the `rescan`/`scan` path) calls the same `_scan_image_in_container` with no mounts, because an arbitrary image has no stack volumes to mount.

Only the online osv-scanner archive scan can abort anything: pip-audit's JSON has no severity field at all, so its findings are reported as `unknown` severity inside the always-exit-0 advisory summary and never reach `gate()` — the CVSS >= HIGH decision exists only in scan.py's Python gate over osv-scanner's `--format json` output.

`install.refs:` carries content pins as DATA in recipe.yaml, validated at load by `_parse_install_refs`: keys match `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$` so the key→env mapping stays a total `.upper()`, `repo` is `owner/repo` (never a URL — the script composes it), `ref` must match `_IMMUTABLE_REF_RE` (a version tag or a full 40-hex commit SHA), and a per-ref `hold:` must be a non-empty reason. `emit.install_env` renders each key to exactly `HARNESSED_REF_<KEY>` and `HARNESSED_REPO_<KEY>` (identical in host and container); `install.cache` is DERIVED from the refs (sha256 of the byte-order-sorted `key=repo@ref` renderings, first 16 hex), so declaring a hand-written `cache:` alongside `refs:` is a schema error and `refs` without `install.script` is also an error; the install script reads pins only from env, `:?`-guarded so an unset ref fails loudly instead of defaulting to the default branch.

`_mutable_archive_ref` treats a github/codeload archive URL as a clone by another spelling (bd harnessed-po7: swapping a SHA for `archive/main.tar.gz` left every pin test green) and asks whether the ref can be PROVEN immutable: `refs/tags/`-qualified refs pass, a NAMED shell variable resolves one hop against `install.refs:` FIRST and literal assignments in the body SECOND (the script's own assignment wins, mirroring shell precedence), an unresolvable variable is reported fail-closed, and a positional parameter passes through — the residual gap mikes-universal-setup closed by naming the variable on each archive URL line, which turned the pass-through into an actual check.

The same floating/clone/archive/fetch pin gates run over `install.script` and `setup.script` bodies via `_lint_script_file` with the recipe threaded in, so `HARNESSED_REF_*` resolves against `install.refs:` there too — moving a pin out of a recipe Dockerfile into a script cannot move it out of enforcement (validate_pin covers the Dockerfile half before anything is emitted).

mikes-universal-setup declares a recipe-wide `install.hold` (bd harnessed-c5t) whose rationale is about what the content IS: a skill is agent instructions executed with the agent's full tool permissions, so a compromised upgrade is prompt injection, not a CVE — no scanner in the osv/trivy/grype family vets it, and a bump requires a human to read the diff. Each ref also carries its own `hold:` naming its class (oakoss: structural — no releases or tags exist; aminblg: policy — SHA-pinned by design), and the recipe-wide hold is the floor: a ref added later without its own hold is still held. `harnessed update` keeps held pins out of the bump set, and `--check` exits non-zero ONLY for a stale, unheld, resolvable, past-cooldown pin — held, cooling, and unresolvable pins are reported without failing.

The repo-root `skills-lock.json` is the vercel `skills` CLI lock format (skill name → source, skillPath, computedHash) and is the INTENDED end state for third-party skill fetching, not the current mechanism: the CLI cannot pin to a SHA (`add repo#<sha>` clones a branch, failing on commits) and does NOT verify computedHash on restore (proven 2026-07-24 — experimental_install installs despite a wrong hash), so a lock file written today would record an unpinned, unverified fetch from a mutable branch (the gsd-build exposure, whose compromised upstream moved tags); until upstream lands SHA pinning (#1439) and verify (#463/#549), mikes-universal-setup's install.sh supplies the pin+verify the ecosystem lacks — bd harnessed-197.

The CI pin check (`.github/workflows/pin-check.yml`) runs `harnessed update --check` over the catalog as a WEEKLY SCHEDULED workflow (Mondays 06:00 UTC, plus manual dispatch), deliberately NOT on pull_request because it resolves live registries and would red an unrelated contributor's branch the moment a third party published — a failing scheduled run is the notification instead. The runner installs mise so backend-prefix pins resolve through `mise registry` to dated upstream releases rather than degrading to reported-but-unchecked `unresolved` rows; the check exits non-zero only for a pin that is stale AND past the minimum release age AND not held (bd harnessed-tfm, harnessed-7zb, harnessed-4xu), with held/cooling/unresolvable pins reported without failing (bd harnessed-c5t).

`tools/scan-real-run.sh` is the real-execution layer for the scan story: it runs the actual `catalog/base/harnessed-scan` against a fake `$HOME` with stub scanners (osv-scanner stubbed to exit 128, snyk stubbed to report the two brace-expansion advisories every published npm bundles) and asserts on the printed summary — exit 0 whatever it found (advisory, never gates), the 128 recorded as a reasoned skip rather than a spurious 'produced NO parseable output' warning, acknowledged advisories printed by name but excluded from the totals, and scan-report.json agreeing with the summary. Stubs rather than real scanners keep the evidence reproducible without live credentials or network.
